5	/// One labelled row: the mark gutter, the leading label column, then the
6	/// controls, then the mixed badge when the selection disagrees. Every pane
7	/// builds rows through here so the label column lines up down the whole
8	/// inspector.
9	///
10	/// The gutter (spec §11 CI-7) is on EVERY row, blank when the row has
11	/// nothing to say, and no spacing follows it, so every control column sits
12	/// exactly `InspectorMetrics.markGutter` right of where it was. `writes` and
13	/// `follows` are the ops the row writes and the ones whose keys it only
14	/// follows; `binding` is what the gutter asks about the selected action. A
15	/// popup, a checkbox or a segmented control is DISCRETE: keyed, it switches
16	/// at the action's end, and the row says "at end"; `discrete: true` says so
17	/// for a row whose control is none of those (a string field or text area,
18	/// which switches at the end too). `default` is the row's
19	/// reset (spec §11 CI-9): a row without one has no reset item in its menu
20	/// and counts nothing toward its section's `differs`.
21	func inspectorRow(
22	    _ label: String?, _ controls: [NSView], mixed: (() -> Bool)? = nil,
23	    binding: InspectorBinding? = nil, writes: [ReelOp] = [], follows: [ReelOp] = [],
24	    discrete forced: Bool = false, default rowDefault: InspectorRowDefault? = nil
25	) -> InspectorRowView {
26	    let field = label.map { InspectorRowLabel($0) }
27	    let discrete = forced || controls.contains {
28	        $0 is OptionPopupControl || $0 is OptionCheckboxControl || $0 is OptionSegmentedControl
29	    }
30	    let gutter = InspectorMarkGutter(
31	        binding: binding, writes: writes, follows: follows, label: field, controls: controls,
32	        discrete: discrete, default: rowDefault)
33	    // The CONTROL gives way, never the tag (G-34 (l), O8): the row's widest
34	    // popup keeps its width only below the one-line tag's compression
35	    // resistance (750), so a keyed row short of room — Font ▸ Family's 150,
36	    // a filter's kind — narrows that popup to show "at end" whole. With no
37	    // tag showing the row has room and the popup is its full width. A row
38	    // with no popup gives its widest checkbox the same 749, so a module's
39	    // boolean with a long label narrows and the tag stays whole; the checkbox
40	    // draws its title from a point, so it is clipped to its own bounds rather
41	    // than drawing on under the tag.
42	    let popups: [NSView] = controls.compactMap { $0 as? OptionPopupControl }
43	    let checks: [NSView] = controls.compactMap { $0 as? OptionCheckboxControl }
44	    if let narrowing = (popups.isEmpty ? checks : popups)
45	        .max(by: { $0.intrinsicContentSize.width < $1.intrinsicContentSize.width })
46	    {
47	        narrowing.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(
48	            NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(749), for: .horizontal)
49	        if narrowing is OptionCheckboxControl { narrowing.clipsToBounds = true }
50	    }
51	    // A one-line name field takes the row's width, whatever its text's
52	    // (spec §11 G-48): it hugs nothing, and it resists compression below the
53	    // tag's 750, so a keyed row narrows the field to show "at end" whole and
54	    // a long text scrolls inside it rather than widening the row.
55	    for name in controls.compactMap({ $0 as? InspectorNameField }) {
56	        name.setContentHuggingPriority(NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
57	        name.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(
58	            NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(248), for: .horizontal)
59	    }
60	    var views: [NSView] = [gutter]
61	    if let field {
62	        field.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
63	        field.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: InspectorMetrics.labelWidth).isActive = true
64	        views.append(field)
65	    }
66	    views.append(contentsOf: controls)
67	    views.append(
68	        InspectorRowTag(
69	            text: { [weak gutter] in gutter?.mark == .keyedAtEnd ? "at end" : nil },
70	            color: DS.action))
71	    if let mixed = mixed { views.append(InspectorMixedBadge(mixed: mixed)) }
72	    // A slider is the row's stretchy element, so a row that has one gets NO
73	    // trailing spacer — two views hugging at the same priority would split
74	    // the free space and leave the slider half as wide as it should be. The
75	    // Content area, a one-line name field (G-48), the Wheels row (GR-11), the
76	    // Curves row (GR-12) and a qualifier range's strip (GR-13) stretch the
77	    // same way.
78	    if !controls.contains(where: {
79	        $0 is InspectorSliderControl || $0 is InspectorTextArea || $0 is InspectorNameField
80	            || $0 is ColorWheelsView || $0 is CurvesView || $0 is RangeStripControl
81	    }) {
82	        let trailing = NSView()
83	        trailing.setContentHuggingPriority(NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
84	        trailing.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(
85	            NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
86	        views.append(trailing)
87	    }
88	    return InspectorRowView(views: views, gutter: gutter)
89	}

108	/// A number bound to one property: a slider that drags LIVE beside a field
109	/// that commits once (spec §4.3). `ops` turns a value into the edit — the
110	/// binding decides whether that is a `set_video` or an action's end patch, so
111	/// no pane repeats that rule.
112	///
113	/// The four typed builders derive the row's default from `read` and `ops`
114	/// (spec §11 CI-9); `resets: false` is for a row whose `read` bypasses the
115	/// props readers, where a derived default could never differ.
116	///
117	/// `sliderMax` gives the slider a shorter travel than the field's `max`, for
118	/// a range whose top would crowd the useful part of a linear rail (Volume,
119	/// spec §11 AU-1): a value past it pins the knob at the rail's end, and a
120	/// drag writes the rail's own range.
121	func inspectorValueRow(
122	    _ label: String, _ binding: InspectorBinding, name: String, unit: String = "",
123	    decimals: Int = 0, min lower: Double, max upper: Double, sliderMax: Double? = nil,
124	    quick: [Double] = [],
125	    slider: Bool = true, width: CGFloat = InspectorMetrics.fieldWidth,
126	    read: @escaping () -> Double, ops: @escaping (Double) -> [ReelOp],
127	    mixed: (() -> Bool)? = nil, enabled: @escaping () -> Bool = { true },
128	    resets: Bool = true
129	) -> NSView {
130	    var controls: [NSView] = []
131	    let track = slider ? InspectorSliderControl(
132	        min: lower, max: sliderMax ?? upper, read: read,
133	        write: { [weak binding] value in binding?.liveUpdate(ops(value)) },
134	        begin: { [weak binding] in binding?.liveBegin() },
135	        end: { [weak binding] in binding?.liveEnd(name) },
136	        enabled: enabled,
137	        start: { [weak binding] in binding?.startValue(read) },
138	        now: { [weak binding] in binding?.nowValue(read) }) : nil
139	    if let track { controls.append(track) }
140	    controls.append(
141	        OptionFieldControl(
142	            width: width, unit: unit, decimals: decimals, min: lower, max: upper, quick: quick,
143	            read: read,
144	            write: { [weak binding] value in binding?.apply(name, ops(value)) },
145	            enabled: enabled,
146	            onEdit: { [weak binding] in binding?.edited() }))
147	    // A field-only row has no rail to put the playhead's tick on, so it says
148	    // the value in words when it differs by more than half a display unit.
149	    if !slider {
150	        controls.append(
151	            InspectorRowTag(
152	                text: { [weak binding] in
153	                    guard let value = binding?.nowValue(read),
154	                          abs(value - read()) > 0.5 * pow(10, -Double(decimals))
155	                    else { return nil }
156	                    return "now " + String(format: "%.\(decimals)f", value) + unit
157	                },
158	                color: DS.playhead))
159	    }
160	    let row = inspectorRow(
161	        label, controls, mixed: mixed, binding: binding, writes: ops(read()),
162	        default: resets ? .derived(binding, name: name, read: read, ops: ops) : nil)
163	    let gutter = row.gutter
164	    track?.keyed = { [weak gutter] in gutter?.isKeyed == true }
165	    return row
166	}

318	/// The colour as the model's RGBA, or nil when it already matches `current`.
319	///
320	/// **Pitfall:** the shared colour panel is continuous, so a drag inside it
321	/// calls a swatch's writer on every mouse-moved event — including with the
322	/// colour it already has. Without this guard the document would answer an
323	/// unchanged edit with a refusal beep on every one of them.
324	func changedRGBA(_ color: NSColor, from current: RGBA) -> RGBA? {
325	    let next = color.rgbaComponents
326	    guard next.count == current.count else { return next }
327	    for (a, b) in zip(next, current) where abs(a - b) > 0.001 { return next }
328	    return nil
329	}

333	/// sentence, VERBATIM, when the core refused a person's edit.
334	/// `ProjectDocument.applyEdit` has already beeped; this is the one thing a
335	/// person sees that an identity does not show them.
336	///
337	/// It lasts until the PROJECT changes — `clearIfStale` runs at the top of
338	/// every inspector refresh and clears it once `editedProject` is another
339	/// handle, which is an applied edit, an undo, a redo or a scope change — or
340	/// until it is clicked. A playhead or selection move keeps the same handle,
341	/// so it keeps the strip. Hidden, it is detached from the foot's stack, so
342	/// it takes no room.

344	    private(set) var text: String?
345	    /// The handle the refusal was shown under. Weak: a handle nothing else
346	    /// holds is one the project has moved away from, and nil is not it.
347	    private weak var project: ReelProject?
348	    private let label = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
349	    /// Its width pinned to the foot's, made on a show: hidden, the strip is
350	    /// detached from the foot's stack, and a constraint made once in
351	    /// `loadView` need not survive that.
352	    private var spanning: NSLayoutConstraint?
353	
354	    init() {
355	        super.init(frame: .zero)
356	        wantsLayer = true
357	        isHidden = true
358	        label.font = DS.sans(11)

360	        label.isSelectable = false
361	        label.maximumNumberOfLines = 3

363	        label.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.defaultLow, for: .horizontal)
364	        label.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false

367	            label.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: topAnchor, constant: 8),
368	            label.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bottomAnchor, constant: -8),

370	                equalTo: leadingAnchor, constant: InspectorMetrics.inset),

content.content:
## Opening Settings

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,). It works with or without a project
open, so you can set keys from the Welcome window before you make anything.
The Assistant tab also opens it for you: when no Anthropic key is set, it
shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an
**Open Settings…** button. The Generate Captions sheet only tells you where
to go: with AssemblyAI chosen and no key set, the note under its button reads
"No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸
Transcription.", and **Generate** shows the same sentence when you rest the
pointer on it.

### What each key turns on

Anything that sends your words or your audio to a language model or a cloud
model needs your own key for it, and without the key the command is greyed
rather than hidden:

- **Your AssemblyAI key** (Transcription, below) turns on the AssemblyAI
  engine of **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and the **Transcribe** buttons of
  **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. With no key, **Generate** is greyed when
  the AssemblyAI engine is chosen (unless every file is already transcribed,
  see [Captions](captions.md)), each **Transcribe** button is greyed, and
  **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** itself is greyed and reads **Remove Filler
  Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)** — unless a file in the project already
  has a transcript made with filler words, which it keeps using without a
  key.
- **Your Anthropic key** (Assistant, below) turns on the assistant. With no
  key, **View ▸ Assistant** still opens the Assistant tab, which says how to
  add the key.

Resting the pointer on a greyed control shows "No AssemblyAI API key is set.
Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." (or the same sentence for
Anthropic and **Assistant**). Saving the key turns the commands on at once,
even with the sheet still open; there is nothing to relaunch. Everything that
runs on your Mac — on-device captions, Remove Silences, Enhance Voice and the
rest — needs no key.

Settings is one window, not a set of tabs. It holds four sections, top to
bottom: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. On a
short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls. Closing it
loses nothing: every control saves as you use it, or when you press its
**Save** button, as described below. While it is open it is listed in the
**Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.

The Assistant, Transcription and Playback headings each carry an ⓘ button.
Rest the pointer on it for a moment to see that section's explanation; click
it to keep the explanation open, and click it again (or anywhere else, or
press Escape) to close it.

*Agents:* no MCP tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Keys, the model,
the region and Background render are set only by a person in this window.
An agent's cloud tools (`transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine,
`transcribe_for_fillers`) do use the key and region saved here, so a person
must set the key first; without one they refuse, at the point they would
send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸
Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use is answered
without a key. The assistant's own tool, `assistant_send` (a dev tool), refuses
the same way with the Anthropic sentence.

## MCP
  installs one without asking you.

Every update is signed, and Frame Job refuses one whose signature does not
match the key built into the app, so only a release published from the
project itself can be installed. Updates are always the whole app; release
notes are on the release's page on GitHub.

There is no Settings control for automatic checks. Your answer is kept in
macOS's preferences for Frame Job (below); to turn checks off later, run
`defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool NO` in
Terminal while Frame Job is closed, and **Check for Updates…** still works.

*Agents:* no MCP tool checks for or installs updates.

## View settings Frame Job remembers
### How keys are stored

Each key is a plain file, readable and writable only by your user account
(mode `0600`). It is written to a temporary name and renamed into place, so
it never exists with looser permissions and is never half-written. Keys are
never put in macOS preferences, never logged, never passed as a launch
argument and never shown in the window again. Frame Job does not use the
Keychain. Anything running as your user account can read these files, so
treat your Mac account as the protection.

### Keys from the environment

If no key is stored, Frame Job falls back to an environment variable, which
is useful when you launch it from a terminal:

| Key | Variable |
|---|---|
| Anthropic (Assistant) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| AssemblyAI (Transcription) | `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` |

A stored key always wins over the variable. An empty variable counts as no
key. **Verify** checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or stored.

## Limits
## Privacy: what leaves your Mac

When you use the assistant, these go to Anthropic, under your key:

- your messages, and the context block in front of each one (the project's name and path, the open nest, the playhead, the selection)
- what the tools answer: the project's details as JSON (including media file paths), clip transcripts it reads, refusals and other results
- the frames it renders to look at the picture

Frame Job doesn't send any of this anywhere else. Audio never goes to the cloud transcriber from the assistant (see [Tools it will not call](#tools-it-will-not-call)). The assistant asks before it exports a movie or captions, saves the project, or consolidates media; other tools can still write files without asking (a rendered frame's PNG, and graphics modules, fonts and assets in the project's package). Once a day at most, the helper downloads LiteLLM's public price table from GitHub. That request carries no key and no project data.

Everything else stays on your Mac: the key file, the spend ledger and the cached price table, `anthropic-prices.json`, all in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. The conversation itself is kept in memory only, and goes when you clear it or close the window.

## Limits

- The assistant works only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation.
- It needs your own Anthropic API key. There is no Frame Job account or relay.
- It can't record the screen, close its window's project, or send audio to the cloud transcriber.
- A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse.
- Stop doesn't cancel an export that has already been queued.
- With compaction off, a long conversation eventually fails until you **Clear** it.
- Changing the key or the model ends every window's conversation.

*Agents:* none. The Assistant is the person's own conversation, and its settings are deliberately out of reach of any tool. An agent drives the same tools directly over [MCP](mcp.md), and is never asked first or refused by the assistant's rules above.

## Saving, reverting and closing

| Command | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **File ▸ New Project** | ⌘N | A blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project. |
| **File ▸ Open…** | ⌘O | Opens a package, or builds an untitled project around a movie, sound file or picture. |
| **File ▸ Open Recent ▸** | | Recently opened projects; **Clear Menu** empties the list. |
| **File ▸ Close** | ⌘W | Closes the window. A project that has been saved writes its changes and closes without asking; an untitled project with changes (an opened movie always counts) asks whether to save first. |
| **File ▸ Save** | ⌘S | Writes the package. An untitled project asks where. |
| **File ▸ Save As…** | ⇧⌘S | Writes the project to a new package. |
| **File ▸ Revert To ▸** | | Goes back to the last saved version, or browses earlier versions of the package. |

Once a project has been saved it autosaves in place, the macOS way: changes are written to the package as you work, and the package is written beside the old one and swapped in, so a crash part-way through a save cannot leave half a package behind. Because of this, macOS adds its standard document commands to the File menu: **Duplicate**, **Rename…**, **Move To…**, **Revert To ▸** (in place of Revert to Saved) and **Share**, and the same Rename and Move To controls appear when you click the window's title. A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. Making a movie or a still is a separate step; see [Export](export.md).

## Preview canvas gestures

| Gesture | What it does |
|---|---|
| Click a clip | Selects it. ⇧-click adds it to the selection or removes it |
| Click empty canvas | Deselects everything and leaves crop mode. With ⇧, keeps the selection |
| Drag a clip | Moves the selected clips. They snap to the canvas centre, edges and thirds and to other layers. ⌘ turns snapping off |
| Drag a corner or side handle | Scales. Video, image, still, graphic and nest clips always scale uniformly. On a shape, ⇧ on a corner handle frees the aspect ratio and a side handle changes only the width or the height. On a text clip, the left and right handles set the wrap width. ⌥ scales around the centre. See [Move, scale and rotate](canvas-and-layers.md#move-scale-and-rotate) |
| Drag the rotation handle | Rotates. ⇧ snaps to 15° steps |
| Drag a crop handle (crop mode) | Crops |
| Drag a line or arrow endpoint | Moves that end of the shape |
| Drag an obscure region's centre grip or one of its eight handles | Moves or resizes that region. ⌥ resizes it around its centre. The grips show only with exactly one unlocked clip selected, outside crop mode. A drag inside the region but away from the grips still moves the clip |
| Double-click a text clip | Edits the text in place |
| Double-click any other clip | Turns on crop mode |
| ← → ↑ ↓ (canvas has focus) | Moves the selected clips 1 pixel. With ⇧, 10 pixels |
| Hold Space and drag | Pans a zoomed canvas that is larger than the preview. A Space tap still plays and pauses |
| Pinch, or ⌥ / ⌘ with the scroll wheel | Steps the canvas zoom |
| Scroll | Pans a canvas that is larger than the preview |

Clips on locked tracks don't move. When an action is selected, a drag or an
arrow-key nudge sets the value at that action's end, not the clip's own
value. See [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md).

*Agents:* `set_video` (position, scale, rotation, crop), `set_shape`,
`set_text`.

"""The documentation site (`docs/site/`) against the tree. No app, no build, no network, stdlib
only; `pnpm build` in `docs/site/` is what proves the site renders and its links land.

A user-visible change has to reach the site, and nothing about the site's build notices a menu
item or an agent tool it has never heard of. These rows do:

  D1  every page has a title and a description;
  D2  the sidebar and the pages are one-to-one;
  D3  every feature in `src/data/features.json` names a page, and an anchor that page has;
  D4  every product tool in `AgentCatalog*.swift` has a heading on an `mcp/` page, and no dev tool
      (`AgentServer+DevTools.swift`) is named anywhere;
  D5  every menu item in `AppDelegate+*Menu*.swift` and `EditorViewController+GraphicMenus.swift`
      is on a reference page;
  D6  no page names something internal: a decision ID, a road map, an `rc_*` export, a source

  D7  no page or data file holds a local path;
  D8  every `<Shot>` names a capture that exists in both looks;
  D9  no page uses the words `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` bans.

    python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py                       # the tree (make test)

17	## Add a marker
18	
19	Move the playhead to the moment and press <kbd>M</kbd>. The bookmark button in the timeline bar and **Mark ▸ Add Marker** do the same.
20	
21	A new marker is red and is called `Marker 1`, `Marker 2` and so on. Two markers can't share a frame, so pressing <kbd>M</kbd> on a frame that already has one beeps and adds nothing.
22	
23	A marker draws on the ruler as a small flag with a thin line down the ruler, in its colour. An ordinary marker's flag is an outline, and a [chapter](#make-a-chapter) marker's is filled. A project can hold up to 1,024 markers.
24	
25	## Move, rename and remove a marker
26	
27	| To | Do this |
28	| --- | --- |
29	| Move a marker | Drag its flag along the ruler. It snaps, and it won't land on a frame that already has a marker. |
30	| Rename a marker | Double-click its flag, or type in its row in the Document tab. |
31	| Remove a marker | Choose **Delete** in its row in the Document tab. |
32	
33	Each of these is one undo step.
34	
35	Double-clicking a flag opens a field on the ruler. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves the name. <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, and saving an empty field does nothing. The name field in the Document tab is different: empty it and the marker has no name, and the field shows **Marker** in grey.
36	
37	## Jump between markers
38	
39	**Mark ▸ Next Marker** and **Mark ▸ Previous Marker** pause playback and move the playhead to the marker. Neither has a keyboard shortcut. They beep when there's no marker further in that direction, and they're dimmed when the project has no markers.
40	
41	You can also choose **Go** in a marker's row in the Document tab.
42	
43	## The Markers list
44	
45	The **Markers** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) lists every marker in time order, with its time, its name, **Chapter**, **Go** and **Delete**. With no markers it reads "No markers. Press M to add one."
46	
47	## Make a chapter
...
49	A marker's colour can only be set by an agent, with `add_marker` or `set_marker`. The colour names are the six [clip label](/timeline/names-and-labels/) colours, and any other name draws the marker in the neutral text colour.
50	
51	## Good to know
52	
53	Markers belong to the whole timeline, not to a nest. While a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open:
54	
55	- The ruler shows no markers, and drags don't snap to them.
56	- The three marker commands in the **Mark** menu are off, and pressing <kbd>M</kbd> beeps.
57	- **Go** is disabled, because the playhead inside a nest counts from the nest's own start. Its tooltip says to leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>.
58	- The Document tab's list still shows every marker, and its name field, **Chapter** and **Delete** still work.
59	
60	An agent works to the same rule. With a nest open it can't add a marker or move one, but it can rename one, change its colour or chapter setting, or remove it. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
61	
62	## Related
63	
64	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
65	- [The in and out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
66	- [Chapters](/export/chapters/)

---
title: Inspector fields
description: How the inspector's number fields, sliders, colour swatches, Reset buttons and right-click menus behave, with one clip selected or several.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Every control in the [inspector](/getting-started/inspector/) works the same way, whichever tab or section it's in. Learn these once and they apply everywhere.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['↩', 'Tab', '⎋']}
  where={['Every row of the inspector', 'A section header, for Reset', 'Right-click a row']}
  tools="set_action_end"
/>

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Transform section of the inspector. Scale, Rotation, Opacity and Motion Blur each have a slider beside a number field with a chevron at its right. Position X and Position Y are number fields reading 0 px with no slider or chevron. Blend is a pop-up reading Normal."
/>

## Type a value

Click a number field. The value and its unit, such as `24 px`, change to the bare number, selected so your typing replaces it. You can type the unit too if you like.

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Apply the value | Press <kbd>↩</kbd>, keypad Enter or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click anywhere else |
| Throw your typing away and keep the old value | Press <kbd>⎋</kbd> |

All of these give the keyboard back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away. <kbd>Tab</kbd> ends your typing. It doesn't move to the next field unless Full Keyboard Access is on. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).

- A number past the field's range is held to the end of the range.
- Text that isn't a number changes nothing, and the field goes back to the value it had. Decimals take a full stop, whatever your Mac's region.
- An unchanged value isn't an edit, so clicking into a field and leaving makes no undo step.

Three other kinds of field work a little differently:

| Field | How it behaves |
| --- | --- |
| One-line text, such as a clip's name | Takes the whole width of its row, and long text scrolls inside it. <kbd>↩</kbd>, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click elsewhere applies it. |
| Timecode, such as **In** and **Out** in the Clip tab's [Timing section](/editing/timing-section/) | Takes a time such as `1:23`, `83.5` or `1:23:04`. A time Frame Job can't read beeps and the field goes back. A time past what the clip allows isn't held to a range. The edit is [refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/) instead. |
| Multi-line text, such as the Text tab's **Content** | <kbd>↩</kbd> applies and <kbd>⇧↩</kbd> starts a new line. See [Multi-line fields](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/#multi-line-fields). |

A greyed control is dimmed and takes no clicks. It usually depends on something else in its section, such as a shadow's **Blur** waiting for **Drop shadow** to be on.

## Use a quick pick

A field with common values has a chevron at its right. Click the chevron for a menu of those values, each spelled as the field shows it at rest, with a checkmark on the current one. The Shadow section's **Opacity**, for example, offers `0%`, `25%`, `50%`, `75%` and `100%`.

Anything you were typing in the field is applied before the menu opens. Picking the value the field already holds changes nothing and makes no undo step.

## Drag a slider

Click a slider to jump to that value, or drag to follow the pointer. The preview follows as you go, and the whole press, from mouse-down to mouse-up, is one undo step. A press that never changes the value makes no step.

A slider and its field show the same value, but the field can reach further. **Volume**'s slider stops at 400%, for example, while its field goes higher. A value past the slider's end pins the knob at the end of the rail.

With an action selected, a slider also shows where the value starts and where it is at the playhead. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## Choose a colour

Click a colour swatch to open the macOS colour panel. The panel has an opacity control, and the value follows it live, so a drag in the panel changes the picture as you go. A colour you can see through shows a checkerboard in its swatch.

The panel edits the swatch you clicked last. Click another swatch to move it there.

## Edit several clips at once

With several clips selected, the inspector shows the first clip's values. A row whose clips disagree adds a small **mixed** badge beside its control, and resting the pointer on it reads "The selected clips have different values".

The control stays live. An edit gives every selected clip the same value, as one undo step, and the badge goes.

A row writes only to the clips it applies to. With a video clip and a text clip selected, a text setting changes the text clip and leaves the video clip alone.

The [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) works the same way.

## Reset a section

A **Reset** button appears on a section's header only while that section differs from its default. Click it to put the whole section back, as one undo step. Clicking the button doesn't fold the section, though a click anywhere else on the header does.

Not every section has one. While you're editing an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/), Reset is hidden, and the same place shows **Clear** while the action changes something in that section.

## Right-click a row

Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them, for the items that apply to that row.

| Item | When it shows | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action |
| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action |
| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default |
| **Set end value to default** | Takes the place of **Reset to default** while an action is selected, on a row that animates | Sets the row's value at the action's end to the default |

The last two are greyed while the row already holds its default. A row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.

---
title: Inspector fields
description: How the inspector's number fields, sliders, colour swatches, Reset buttons and right-click menus behave, with one clip selected or several.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Every control in the [inspector](/getting-started/inspector/) works the same way, whichever tab or section it's in. Learn these once and they apply everywhere.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['↩', 'Tab', '⎋']}
  where={['Every row of the inspector', 'A section header, for Reset', 'Right-click a row']}
  tools="set_action_end"
/>

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Transform section of the inspector. Scale, Rotation, Opacity and Motion Blur each have a slider beside a number field with a chevron at its right. Position X and Position Y are number fields reading 0 px with no slider or chevron. Blend is a pop-up reading Normal."
/>

## Type a value

Click a number field. The value and its unit, such as `24 px`, change to the bare number, selected so your typing replaces it. You can type the unit too if you like.

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Apply the value | Press <kbd>↩</kbd>, keypad Enter or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click anywhere else |
| Throw your typing away and keep the old value | Press <kbd>⎋</kbd> |

All of these give the keyboard back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away. <kbd>Tab</kbd> ends your typing. It doesn't move to the next field unless Full Keyboard Access is on. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).

- A number past the field's range is held to the end of the range.
- Text that isn't a number changes nothing, and the field goes back to the value it had. Decimals take a full stop, whatever your Mac's region.
- An unchanged value isn't an edit, so clicking into a field and leaving makes no undo step.

Three other kinds of field work a little differently:

| Field | How it behaves |
| --- | --- |
| One-line text, such as a clip's name | Takes the whole width of its row, and long text scrolls inside it. <kbd>↩</kbd>, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click elsewhere applies it. |
| Timecode, such as **In** and **Out** in the Clip tab's [Timing section](/editing/timing-section/) | Takes a time such as `1:23`, `83.5` or `1:23:04`. A time Frame Job can't read beeps and the field goes back. A time past what the clip allows isn't held to a range. The edit is [refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/) instead. |
| Multi-line text, such as the Text tab's **Content** | <kbd>↩</kbd> applies and <kbd>⇧↩</kbd> starts a new line. See [Multi-line fields](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/#multi-line-fields). |

A greyed control is dimmed and takes no clicks. It usually depends on something else in its section, such as a shadow's **Blur** waiting for **Drop shadow** to be on.

## Use a quick pick

A field with common values has a chevron at its right. Click the chevron for a menu of those values, each spelled as the field shows it at rest, with a checkmark on the current one. The Shadow section's **Opacity**, for example, offers `0%`, `25%`, `50%`, `75%` and `100%`.

Anything you were typing in the field is applied before the menu opens. Picking the value the field already holds changes nothing and makes no undo step.

## Drag a slider

Click a slider to jump to that value, or drag to follow the pointer. The preview follows as you go, and the whole press, from mouse-down to mouse-up, is one undo step. A press that never changes the value makes no step.

A slider and its field show the same value, but the field can reach further. **Volume**'s slider stops at 400%, for example, while its field goes higher. A value past the slider's end pins the knob at the end of the rail.

With an action selected, a slider also shows where the value starts and where it is at the playhead. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## Choose a colour

Click a colour swatch to open the macOS colour panel. The panel has an opacity control, and the value follows it live, so a drag in the panel changes the picture as you go. A colour you can see through shows a checkerboard in its swatch.

The panel edits the swatch you clicked last. Click another swatch to move it there.

## Edit several clips at once

With several clips selected, the inspector shows the first clip's values. A row whose clips disagree adds a small **mixed** badge beside its control, and resting the pointer on it reads "The selected clips have different values".

The control stays live. An edit gives every selected clip the same value, as one undo step, and the badge goes.

A row writes only to the clips it applies to. With a video clip and a text clip selected, a text setting changes the text clip and leaves the video clip alone.

The [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) works the same way.

## Reset a section

A **Reset** button appears on a section's header only while that section differs from its default. Click it to put the whole section back, as one undo step. Clicking the button doesn't fold the section, though a click anywhere else on the header does.

Not every section has one. While you're editing an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/), Reset is hidden, and the same place shows **Clear** while the action changes something in that section.

## Right-click a row

Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them, for the items that apply to that row.

| Item | When it shows | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action |
| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action |
| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default |
| **Set end value to default** | Takes the place of **Reset to default** while an action is selected, on a row that animates | Sets the row's value at the action's end to the default |

The last two are greyed while the row already holds its default. A row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.

---
title: Keys and typing
description: How Frame Job's single-letter keys share the keyboard with text fields, what gives the keys back to the editor, and what Esc leaves.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job plays on <kbd>Space</kbd> and trims on <kbd>W</kbd>, so a letter means one thing on the timeline and another in a text field. The rule is short: the keys belong to the editor unless you're typing or a sheet is open.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['Space', '↩', 'Tab', '⎋']}
  where={['The editor window', 'The Preview Window']}
/>

This page explains how the keys are shared. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) has the full list.

## Single-letter keys

These keys need no modifier and act on the editor window. They also work in the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play or pause |
| <kbd>J</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> <kbd>L</kbd> | Play in reverse, pause, play forward |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Back or forward one frame, ten with <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Previous or next edit point |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | Start or end of the project |
| <kbd>,</kbd> <kbd>.</kbd> | Nudge the selected clips one frame earlier or later, ten with <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
| <kbd>I</kbd> <kbd>O</kbd> | Set In, Set Out |
| <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd> | Trim the start or end to the playhead |
| <kbd>M</kbd> | Add Marker |
| <kbd>T</kbd> | Add a text clip at the playhead |
| <kbd>C</kbd> | Crop mode on or off |
| <kbd>Z</kbd> | Region mode for [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) |
| <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> | Fit Timeline |
| <kbd>N</kbd> | Snapping on or off |
| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Deselect the selected action |

<kbd>⇧</kbd> and Caps Lock still count as no modifier, so Caps Lock doesn't stop these keys. <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⌃</kbd> always make it a different key.

They never fire while you're typing. While a sheet is open none of them works, in either window, so the project can't change underneath the sheet. In the Preview Window they also do nothing while a field in the editor window is still being typed in.

Some menu items have a single-letter key the menu doesn't show. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) gives those too.

### When the focus changes a key

A few places claim keys for themselves while they hold the focus:

| Where the focus is | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| The preview canvas | The arrow keys move the selected clips 1 pixel, or 10 with <kbd>⇧</kbd>. Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> and drag to pan a zoomed canvas. A tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays and pauses. |
| The Transcript tab's text | The arrow keys select words. See [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/). |
| A selected point on a [curve](/color/curves/) | The arrow keys move the point, <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes it and <kbd>⎋</kbd> deselects it. |
| A button, with macOS Full Keyboard Access on | <kbd>Space</kbd> presses the button. |

Everywhere else in the window, <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses wherever the focus is.

## Menu shortcuts

Every shortcut with <kbd>⌘</kbd> belongs to a menu item, so it does exactly what the item does. While the item is greyed out, the shortcut does nothing. That includes every editor command while a sheet is open.

## Start and finish typing

A field takes the keys only when you click in it, or choose a command that opens one for typing, such as **Clip ▸ Rename…** or **View ▸ Assistant**. Nothing else moves the keyboard into a field, so you won't type into one by accident.

Any of these applies what you typed and gives the keys back, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away:

| Do this | Where it works |
| --- | --- |
| Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | A one-line field. Multi-line fields have [their own rule](#multi-line-fields). |
| Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>⇧Tab</kbd> | Any text, including the Assistant's message field |
| Click outside the field | Anywhere in the window. The click still does what it would have done, after the field lets go. |

<kbd>Tab</kbd> doesn't step through fields. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, it does, and walks to the next control instead.

A click on the title bar doesn't end your typing. Neither does a click on the field's own margins, on its [quick-pick chevron](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#use-a-quick-pick) or on a text view's scroller, because they count as part of the field.

While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> and <kbd>Tab</kbd> belong to it.

## Delete keys while you type

These four keys edit the timeline when you're not typing. In a text field their menu items switch off, so the keys keep their usual text meaning and your clips stay safe.

| Key | On the timeline |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>⌫</kbd> | **Delete** |
| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | **Ripple Delete** |
| <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | **Open Nest** |
| <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | **Close Nest** |

## Multi-line fields

Three places take more than one line: the Text tab's **Content**, the Assistant's message field and text you're [editing on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | Applies the text. In the Assistant's message field it sends the message, and beeps if the Assistant is busy. |
| <kbd>↩</kbd> with any of <kbd>⇧</kbd>, <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌃</kbd> | Starts a new line |

On the canvas, <kbd>⎋</kbd> stops editing. If the text changed, Frame Job asks whether to **Apply**, **Revert** or **Cancel**.

While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> belongs to it.

## Keys in a sheet

In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the main button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> presses **Cancel**.

## What Esc leaves

<kbd>⎋</kbd> backs out of whatever is under way.

| What's under way | What <kbd>⎋</kbd> does |
| --- | --- |
| A canvas drag: move, scale, rotate, crop, a line's endpoint or an obscure region | Puts everything back as it was before you pressed, with no undo step |
| Crop mode | Leaves it, as <kbd>↩</kbd> does |
| Region mode, from <kbd>Z</kbd> or the Obscure section's **Place on Canvas** | Leaves it |
| The key-colour or qualifier eyedropper | Cancels it |
| A selected curve point in the Color tab | Deselects it |
| A selected action | Deselects it, so the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again |
| Typing in a number field | Throws the typing away |
| A rename field on the timeline | Closes it and keeps the old name |
| A selection in the Transcript tab | Clears it |

Region mode also ends by itself when the selection stops being the clip it started for, or the playhead leaves that clip.

A canvas tool that waits for your click or drag shows a crosshair and a hint on the canvas, and only one can be armed at a time. The hint says what to do:

- "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel"
- "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel"
- "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel"
- "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel"

## Related

- [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/)
- [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/)
- [Gestures with no menu item](/reference/gestures/)

---
title: Undo and saving
description: What one undo step is, how the Edit menu names it, what makes no step, and how Autosave keeps your work.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every change to a project is a step you can take back. Once a project has been saved, Frame Job also writes your work to disk as you go, so you can try things without worrying about losing it.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Undo', 'Edit ▸ Redo']}
  keys={['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z']}
  tools={['undo', 'redo']}
/>

## Undo and redo

**Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) and **Edit ▸ Redo** (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) walk back and forward one step at a time.

A new edit clears the redo history, so anything you undid and didn't redo is gone. Each project keeps its last 32 steps.

## What counts as one step

One step is one thing you did, however many clips it touched.

| What you did | How much it counts for |
| --- | --- |
| A menu command or key | One step, even when it changes many clips. Ripple Delete over a range, Un-nest of several nests, Detach Audio on a selection and a Remove Silences pass are each one. |
| A gesture | One step from mouse-down to mouse-up, however long the drag lasts: a move, trim, rate stretch, slip, roll or duplicate-drag. |
| An inspector edit | One step for a typed value or a slider press, even with several clips selected. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/). |
| A track switch, a rename or a reorder | Each one is its own step. |

## How steps are named

The Edit menu names the step it will take back, such as **Undo Move Clips**, and Redo is named the same way. Check the name before you press if you're not sure what you're about to undo.

| For | The names you'll see include |
| --- | --- |
| Clips | Move Clips, Rename Clip, Label Clip |
| Tracks | Hide Track, Mute Track, Lock Track, Solo Track, Track Matte, Track Volume, Track Pan, Reset Track Mix, Rename Track, Reorder Track, New Track, Remove Track, Remove Empty Tracks |
| Markers | Add Marker, Move Marker, Rename Marker, Chapter Marker, Remove Marker |

## What makes no step

Anything that doesn't change the project makes no step, so <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> walks straight past it:

- Selecting, including a click on a clip that doesn't move it.
- Moving the playhead.
- Setting the in/out range.
- Going into or out of a nest.
- An edit Frame Job [refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- An edit that would leave everything as it was.

<kbd>⌘Z</kbd> in the Assistant's message field undoes your typing there and never touches the project's steps. Sending the message drops that typing history.

## How Autosave keeps your work

Once a project has been saved, it autosaves in place as you work, the macOS way. An untitled project has no package on disk until its first Save, so save early. See [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/) for Save, **Revert To ▸** and browsing earlier versions.

The word "edited" in the title bar means changes haven't reached the disk yet. It clears after every silent autosave, and the window's close button never shows a dot.

## With an agent

Each agent tool call that edits the project is exactly one step, so one `undo` takes back one call. `undo` reports the name of the step it took back, and it's an error when there's nothing to undo. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

## Related

- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)

---
title: Undo and saving
description: What one undo step is, how the Edit menu names it, what makes no step, and how Autosave keeps your work.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every change to a project is a step you can take back. Once a project has been saved, Frame Job also writes your work to disk as you go, so you can try things without worrying about losing it.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Undo', 'Edit ▸ Redo']}
  keys={['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z']}
  tools={['undo', 'redo']}
/>

## Undo and redo

**Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) and **Edit ▸ Redo** (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) walk back and forward one step at a time.

A new edit clears the redo history, so anything you undid and didn't redo is gone. Each project keeps its last 32 steps.

## What counts as one step

One step is one thing you did, however many clips it touched.

| What you did | How much it counts for |
| --- | --- |
| A menu command or key | One step, even when it changes many clips. Ripple Delete over a range, Un-nest of several nests, Detach Audio on a selection and a Remove Silences pass are each one. |
| A gesture | One step from mouse-down to mouse-up, however long the drag lasts: a move, trim, rate stretch, slip, roll or duplicate-drag. |
| An inspector edit | One step for a typed value or a slider press, even with several clips selected. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/). |
| A track switch, a rename or a reorder | Each one is its own step. |

## How steps are named

The Edit menu names the step it will take back, such as **Undo Move Clips**, and Redo is named the same way. Check the name before you press if you're not sure what you're about to undo.

| For | The names you'll see include |
| --- | --- |
| Clips | Move Clips, Rename Clip, Label Clip |
| Tracks | Hide Track, Mute Track, Lock Track, Solo Track, Track Matte, Track Volume, Track Pan, Reset Track Mix, Rename Track, Reorder Track, New Track, Remove Track, Remove Empty Tracks |
| Markers | Add Marker, Move Marker, Rename Marker, Chapter Marker, Remove Marker |

## What makes no step

Anything that doesn't change the project makes no step, so <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> walks straight past it:

- Selecting, including a click on a clip that doesn't move it.
- Moving the playhead.
- Setting the in/out range.
- Going into or out of a nest.
- An edit Frame Job [refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- An edit that would leave everything as it was.

<kbd>⌘Z</kbd> in the Assistant's message field undoes your typing there and never touches the project's steps. Sending the message drops that typing history.

## How Autosave keeps your work

Once a project has been saved, it autosaves in place as you work, the macOS way. An untitled project has no package on disk until its first Save, so save early. See [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/) for Save, **Revert To ▸** and browsing earlier versions.

The word "edited" in the title bar means changes haven't reached the disk yet. It clears after every silent autosave, and the window's close button never shows a dot.

## With an agent

Each agent tool call that edits the project is exactly one step, so one `undo` takes back one call. `undo` reports the name of the step it took back, and it's an error when there's nothing to undo. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

## Related

- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)

---
title: When an edit is refused
description: How Frame Job tells you it won't make an edit, from the Refused strip in the inspector to a beep with no message, and why nothing changes.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job has rules that keep a project sound, such as how far two clips may overlap. When an edit would break one, nothing changes and Frame Job says so. How it says so tells you what happened.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The foot of the inspector', 'The timeline, for a drop']}
/>

| What you see | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| A beep and a **Refused:** line at the foot of the inspector | A rule wouldn't allow the edit |
| A clip animates back to where it was | The rules refused a drop |
| A beep and no message | The edit would have changed nothing |
| An error alert | Frame Job couldn't use the request at all |

None of these changes the project or makes an undo step.

## The refusal strip

When a rule won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's own sentence at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused: ":

> Refused: track 3 is locked, so the gap on it cannot be closed

The strip shows up to three lines. Rest the pointer on it to read the whole sentence.

It stays until you click it or the project changes, which means an edit, an undo or redo, or going into or out of a nest. Moving the playhead or changing the selection doesn't clear it, so you can look around while you work out what to do.

The sentence is exact rather than friendly. It can name clips and tracks by Frame Job's own numbers, which aren't their positions on the timeline, and give lengths in the timeline's smallest units rather than in seconds.

Each feature's page lists what can stop it, and [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/) gathers them in one place.

A typed Start, Length or end value on an action shows the strip too. Dragging an action's band never does. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

## A drop that springs back

A clip dropped where the rules refuse animates back to where it was, and nothing changes. While you drag, positions that would be refused are skipped and the clip waits at the last allowed one. Only the drop counts. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).

## A beep with no message

An edit that would change nothing beeps but shows no message, because no rule was broken. A slip already at the end of the footage does this, and so does pasting a look the clips already have.

## An error alert

Now and then Frame Job can't use a request at all, such as a value outside its allowed range. It shows an error alert naming the offending value. You'll rarely meet one, because the inspector's number fields already [hold what you type to their range](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#type-a-value).

## With an agent

An agent gets the same answers as words. A refused edit fails with the rule's sentence, and an edit that changes nothing fails saying so. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

## Related

- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)
- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)

---
title: AI features and your own keys
description: Which features need nothing, which use an on-device model, which need your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, and what ever leaves your Mac.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Most of Frame Job needs no key and no network. The few features that send your words or audio to a cloud model run on your own API keys, so you decide what's used and you pay the provider directly.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where={['Settings ▸ Assistant', 'Settings ▸ Transcription']}
  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers']}
  needs="Your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, only for the features that send to them."
/>

## Your own keys

There's no Frame Job account and no relay in between. There are two keys in all, and each provider bills your account directly.

| Key | Turns on | Saved in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | The Assistant | [Settings ▸ Assistant](/assistant/set-up/) |
| AssemblyAI | Cloud captions and Remove Filler Words | [Settings ▸ Transcription](/captions/assemblyai-key/) |

Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each Assistant turn and each month costs. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). The provider's bill is the real figure.

With no key set, Settings says "No API key is set." in its ordinary muted colour. That's a state, not an error.

## What needs what

Anything that sends your words or audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.

| What it takes | Features |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing | Editing, colour, graphics, recording and export |
| An on-device model, with no key and no upload | **Generate Captions** with **On this Mac**, Remove Silences' voice analysis, Enhance Voice and Voice Isolation, Split at Shot Changes, Remove Background, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and Switch by Speaker |
| Your AssemblyAI key | The **AssemblyAI** engine of **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** with its **Transcribe** buttons |
| Your Anthropic key | The Assistant |

Filler removal works only through AssemblyAI. There's no on-device version.

Without your Anthropic key, **View ▸ Assistant** still opens the tab, which says how to add the key.

Work you've already paid for keeps working with no key:

- **Generate** isn't greyed when every file is already transcribed.
- **Remove Filler Words…** stays on while a file it would work on has a current transcript made with filler words.

An on-device language that isn't installed yet shows a **Download** row in the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet.

## Greyed commands

A command that needs a key you haven't set is greyed rather than hidden, and it says which key and where to set it.

A greyed menu item's title gains the key's name, as in **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. Rest the pointer on a greyed command or button and it reads:

> No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.

For the Assistant it's the same sentence with Anthropic and Assistant. The Assistant tab itself reads "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." with an **Open Settings…** button.

An agent's tool stops with the same sentence, at the point it would send. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what still works without a key.

## Saving a key takes effect at once

Saving or removing a key updates open sheets and menu items straight away. An open Generate Captions sheet turns **Generate** back on with the sheet still up, and there's nothing to reopen or relaunch.

## What stays on this Mac

Editing, analysis, on-device transcription, recording and export all stay on this Mac. Only these reach the network, and each is something you start or can see:

| Goes to | What | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AssemblyAI | The audio of the files being transcribed | When you press **Generate** or **Transcribe** with that engine. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/). |
| Anthropic | Your Assistant messages, the project's details and the frames it renders | While you use the Assistant. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/). |
| GitHub | A request for LiteLLM's published price table, with no key and no project data | At most once a day, from the Assistant's helper |
| GitHub | A check of the update feed | In the [downloaded copy](/getting-started/updates/) only |
| Apple | A request for an on-device speech model, through macOS | When you ask for one |

Frame Job has no analytics or telemetry code.

## Related

- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)

---
title: Updates
description: Check for a newer Frame Job, choose whether it checks by itself, and see which copies update themselves.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The copy of Frame Job you download keeps itself up to date. It tells you when a new version is ready and installs it only when you say so.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…"
  needs="The copy downloaded from the project's GitHub Releases page."
/>

## Which copy updates itself

The copy you download from the project's GitHub Releases page updates itself, with [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org). A copy built from source has no updater: it has no menu item and it never checks.

An update is always the whole app. Release notes are on the release's page on GitHub.

## Check for updates

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…**, directly under **About Frame Job**. It has no shortcut.

If a newer Frame Job has been published, a window shows its version and a link to its release page. Choose **Install Update** to replace the app and relaunch it. If there's nothing newer, it says you're up to date.

The item is greyed while a check is already running.

## Automatic checks

The second time you open Frame Job, it asks whether to check for updates automatically. If you agree, it checks about once a day while it's open and tells you when an update is ready. It never installs one without asking.

Frame Job [remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/) your answer and when it last checked.

## Turn automatic checks off

There's no Settings control for this. With Frame Job closed, run this in Terminal:

```sh
defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool NO
```

**Check for Updates…** still works afterwards.

## Signed updates

Every update is signed, and Frame Job refuses one whose signature doesn't match the key built into the app. Only a release published from the project itself can be installed.

## Good to know

No agent tool checks for updates or installs them.

## Related

- [Requirements and install](/getting-started/requirements-and-install/)
- [What stays on this Mac](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/#what-stays-on-this-mac)
- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)

input.content:
---
title: Inspector fields
description: How the inspector's number fields, sliders, colour swatches, Reset buttons and right-click menus behave, with one clip selected or several.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Every control in the [inspector](/getting-started/inspector/) works the same way, whichever tab or section it's in. Learn these once and they apply everywhere.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['↩', 'Tab', '⎋']}
  where={['Every row of the inspector', 'A section header, for Reset', 'Right-click a row']}
  tools="set_action_end"
/>

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Transform section of the inspector. Scale, Rotation, Opacity and Motion Blur each have a slider beside a number field with a chevron at its right. Position X and Position Y are number fields reading 0 px with no slider or chevron. Blend is a pop-up reading Normal."
/>

## Type a value

Click a number field. The value and its unit, such as `24 px`, change to the bare number, selected so your typing replaces it. You can type the unit too if you like.

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Apply the value | Press <kbd>↩</kbd>, keypad Enter or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click anywhere else |
| Throw your typing away and keep the old value | Press <kbd>⎋</kbd> |

All of these give the keyboard back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away. <kbd>Tab</kbd> ends your typing. It doesn't move to the next field unless Full Keyboard Access is on. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).

- A number past the field's range is held to the end of the range.
- Text that isn't a number changes nothing, and the field goes back to the value it had. Decimals take a full stop, whatever your Mac's region.
- An unchanged value isn't an edit, so clicking into a field and leaving makes no undo step.

Three other kinds of field work a little differently:

| Field | How it behaves |
| --- | --- |
| One-line text, such as a clip's name | Takes the whole width of its row, and long text scrolls inside it. <kbd>↩</kbd>, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click elsewhere applies it. |
| Timecode, such as **In** and **Out** in the Clip tab's [Timing section](/editing/timing-section/) | Takes a time such as `1:23`, `83.5` or `1:23:04`. A time Frame Job can't read beeps and the field goes back. A time past what the clip allows isn't held to a range. The edit is [refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/) instead. |
| Multi-line text, such as the Text tab's **Content** | <kbd>↩</kbd> applies and <kbd>⇧↩</kbd> starts a new line. See [Multi-line fields](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/#multi-line-fields). |

A greyed control is dimmed and takes no clicks. It usually depends on something else in its section, such as a shadow's **Blur** waiting for **Drop shadow** to be on.

## Use a quick pick

A field with common values has a chevron at its right. Click the chevron for a menu of those values, each spelled as the field shows it at rest, with a checkmark on the current one. The Shadow section's **Opacity**, for example, offers `0%`, `25%`, `50%`, `75%` and `100%`.

Anything you were typing in the field is applied before the menu opens. Picking the value the field already holds changes nothing and makes no undo step.

## Drag a slider

Click a slider to jump to that value, or drag to follow the pointer. The preview follows as you go, and the whole press, from mouse-down to mouse-up, is one undo step. A press that never changes the value makes no step.

A slider and its field show the same value, but the field can reach further. **Volume**'s slider stops at 400%, for example, while its field goes higher. A value past the slider's end pins the knob at the end of the rail.

With an action selected, a slider also shows where the value starts and where it is at the playhead. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## Choose a colour

Click a colour swatch to open the macOS colour panel. The panel has an opacity control, and the value follows it live, so a drag in the panel changes the picture as you go. A colour you can see through shows a checkerboard in its swatch.

The panel edits the swatch you clicked last. Click another swatch to move it there.

## Edit several clips at once

With several clips selected, the inspector shows the first clip's values. A row whose clips disagree adds a small **mixed** badge beside its control, and resting the pointer on it reads "The selected clips have different values".

The control stays live. An edit gives every selected clip the same value, as one undo step, and the badge goes.

A row writes only to the clips it applies to. With a video clip and a text clip selected, a text setting changes the text clip and leaves the video clip alone.

The [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) works the same way.

## Reset a section

A **Reset** button appears on a section's header only while that section differs from its default. Click it to put the whole section back, as one undo step. Clicking the button doesn't fold the section, though a click anywhere else on the header does.

Not every section has one. While you're editing an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/), Reset is hidden, and the same place shows **Clear** while the action changes something in that section.

## Right-click a row

Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them, for the items that apply to that row.

| Item | When it shows | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action |
| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action |
| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default |
| **Set end value to default** | Takes the place of **Reset to default** while an action is selected, on a row that animates | Sets the row's value at the action's end to the default |

The last two are greyed while the row already holds its default. A row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.

What the marks in a row's left gutter mean is on [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)

---
title: Keys and typing
description: How Frame Job's single-letter keys share the keyboard with text fields, what gives the keys back to the editor, and what Esc leaves.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job plays on <kbd>Space</kbd> and trims on <kbd>W</kbd>, so a letter means one thing on the timeline and another in a text field. The rule is short: the keys belong to the editor unless you're typing or a sheet is open.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['Space', '↩', 'Tab', '⎋']}
  where={['The editor window', 'The Preview Window']}
/>

This page explains how the keys are shared. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) has the full list.

## Single-letter keys

These keys need no modifier and act on the editor window. They also work in the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play or pause |
| <kbd>J</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> <kbd>L</kbd> | Play in reverse, pause, play forward |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Back or forward one frame, ten with <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Previous or next edit point |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | Start or end of the project |
| <kbd>,</kbd> <kbd>.</kbd> | Nudge the selected clips one frame earlier or later, ten with <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
| <kbd>I</kbd> <kbd>O</kbd> | Set In, Set Out |
| <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd> | Trim the start or end to the playhead |
| <kbd>M</kbd> | Add Marker |
| <kbd>T</kbd> | Add a text clip at the playhead |
| <kbd>C</kbd> | Crop mode on or off |
| <kbd>Z</kbd> | Region mode for [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) |
| <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> | Fit Timeline |
| <kbd>N</kbd> | Snapping on or off |
| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Deselect the selected action |

<kbd>⇧</kbd> and Caps Lock still count as no modifier, so Caps Lock doesn't stop these keys. <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⌃</kbd> always make it a different key.

They never fire while you're typing. While a sheet is open none of them works, in either window, so the project can't change underneath the sheet. In the Preview Window they also do nothing while a field in the editor window is still being typed in.

Some menu items have a single-letter key the menu doesn't show. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) gives those too.

### When the focus changes a key

A few places claim keys for themselves while they hold the focus:

| Where the focus is | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| The preview canvas | The arrow keys move the selected clips 1 pixel, or 10 with <kbd>⇧</kbd>. Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> and drag to pan a zoomed canvas. A tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays and pauses. |
| The Transcript tab's text | The arrow keys select words. See [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/). |
| A selected point on a [curve](/color/curves/) | The arrow keys move the point, <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes it and <kbd>⎋</kbd> deselects it. |
| A button, with macOS Full Keyboard Access on | <kbd>Space</kbd> presses the button. |

Everywhere else in the window, <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses wherever the focus is.

## Menu shortcuts

Every shortcut with <kbd>⌘</kbd> belongs to a menu item, so it does exactly what the item does. While the item is greyed out, the shortcut does nothing. That includes every editor command while a sheet is open.

## Start and finish typing

A field takes the keys only when you click in it, or choose a command that opens one for typing, such as **Clip ▸ Rename…** or **View ▸ Assistant**. Nothing else moves the keyboard into a field, so you won't type into one by accident.

Any of these applies what you typed and gives the keys back, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away:

| Do this | Where it works |
| --- | --- |
| Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | A one-line field. Multi-line fields have [their own rule](#multi-line-fields). |
| Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>⇧Tab</kbd> | Any text, including the Assistant's message field |
| Click outside the field | Anywhere in the window. The click still does what it would have done, after the field lets go. |

<kbd>Tab</kbd> doesn't step through fields. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, it does, and walks to the next control instead.

A click on the title bar doesn't end your typing. Neither does a click on the field's own margins, on its [quick-pick chevron](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#use-a-quick-pick) or on a text view's scroller, because they count as part of the field.

While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> and <kbd>Tab</kbd> belong to it.

## Delete keys while you type

These four keys edit the timeline when you're not typing. In a text field their menu items switch off, so the keys keep their usual text meaning and your clips stay safe.

| Key | On the timeline |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>⌫</kbd> | **Delete** |
| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | **Ripple Delete** |
| <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | **Open Nest** |
| <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | **Close Nest** |

## Multi-line fields

Three places take more than one line: the Text tab's **Content**, the Assistant's message field and text you're [editing on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | Applies the text. In the Assistant's message field it sends the message, and beeps if the Assistant is busy. |
| <kbd>↩</kbd> with any of <kbd>⇧</kbd>, <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌃</kbd> | Starts a new line |

On the canvas, <kbd>⎋</kbd> stops editing. If the text changed, Frame Job asks whether to **Apply**, **Revert** or **Cancel**.

While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> belongs to it.

## Keys in a sheet

In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the main button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> presses **Cancel**.

## What Esc leaves

<kbd>⎋</kbd> backs out of whatever is under way.

| What's under way | What <kbd>⎋</kbd> does |
| --- | --- |
| A canvas drag: move, scale, rotate, crop, a line's endpoint or an obscure region | Puts everything back as it was before you pressed, with no undo step |
| Crop mode | Leaves it, as <kbd>↩</kbd> does |
| Region mode, from <kbd>Z</kbd> or the Obscure section's **Place on Canvas** | Leaves it |
| The key-colour or qualifier eyedropper | Cancels it |
| A selected curve point in the Color tab | Deselects it |
| A selected action | Deselects it, so the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again |
| Typing in a number field | Throws the typing away |
| A rename field on the timeline | Closes it and keeps the old name |
| A selection in the Transcript tab | Clears it |

Region mode also ends by itself when the selection stops being the clip it started for, or the playhead leaves that clip.

A canvas tool that waits for your click or drag shows a crosshair and a hint on the canvas, and only one can be armed at a time. The hint says what to do:

- "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel"
- "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel"
- "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel"
- "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel"
