---
title: Undo and saving
description: What one undo step is, how the Edit menu names it, what makes no step, and how Autosave keeps your work.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every change to a project is a step you can take back. Once a project has been saved, Frame Job also writes your work to disk as you go, so you can try things without worrying about losing it.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Undo', 'Edit ▸ Redo']}
  keys={['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z']}
  tools={['undo', 'redo']}
/>

## Undo and redo

**Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) and **Edit ▸ Redo** (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) walk back and forward one step at a time.

A new edit clears the redo history, so anything you undid and didn't redo is gone. Each project keeps its last 32 steps.

## What counts as one step

One step is one thing you did, however many clips it touched.

| What you did | How much it counts for |
| --- | --- |
| A menu command or key | One step, even when it changes many clips. Ripple Delete over a range, Un-nest of several nests, Detach Audio on a selection and a Remove Silences pass are each one. |
| A gesture | One step from mouse-down to mouse-up, however long the drag lasts: a move, trim, rate stretch, slip, roll or duplicate-drag. |
| An inspector edit | One step for a typed value or a slider press, even with several clips selected. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/). |
| A track switch, a rename or a reorder | Each one is its own step. |

## How steps are named

The Edit menu names the step it will take back, such as **Undo Move Clips**, and Redo is named the same way. Check the name before you press if you're not sure what you're about to undo.

| For | The names you'll see include |
| --- | --- |
| Clips | Move Clips, Rename Clip, Label Clip |
| Tracks | Hide Track, Mute Track, Lock Track, Solo Track, Track Matte, Track Volume, Track Pan, Reset Track Mix, Rename Track, Reorder Track, New Track, Remove Track, Remove Empty Tracks |
| Markers | Add Marker, Move Marker, Rename Marker, Chapter Marker, Remove Marker |

## What makes no step

Anything that doesn't change the project makes no step, so <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> walks straight past it:

- Selecting, including a click on a clip that doesn't move it.
- Moving the playhead.
- Setting the in/out range.
- Going into or out of a nest.
- An edit Frame Job [refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- An edit that would leave everything as it was.

<kbd>⌘Z</kbd> in the Assistant's message field undoes your typing there and never touches the project's steps. Sending the message drops that typing history.

## How Autosave keeps your work

Once a project has been saved, it autosaves in place as you work, the macOS way. An untitled project has no package on disk until its first Save, so save early. See [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/) for Save, **Revert To ▸** and browsing earlier versions.

The word "edited" in the title bar means changes haven't reached the disk yet. It clears after every silent autosave, and the window's close button never shows a dot.

## With an agent

Each agent tool call that edits the project is exactly one step, so one `undo` takes back one call. `undo` reports the name of the step it took back, and it's an error when there's nothing to undo. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

## Related

- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)

---
title: When an edit is refused
description: How Frame Job tells you it won't make an edit, from the Refused strip in the inspector to a beep with no message, and why nothing changes.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job has rules that keep a project sound, such as how far two clips may overlap. When an edit would break one, nothing changes and Frame Job says so. How it says so tells you what happened.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The foot of the inspector', 'The timeline, for a drop']}
/>

| What you see | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| A beep and a **Refused:** line at the foot of the inspector | A rule wouldn't allow the edit |
| A clip animates back to where it was | The rules refused a drop |
| A beep and no message | The edit would have changed nothing |
| An error alert | Frame Job couldn't use the request at all |

None of these changes the project or makes an undo step.

## The refusal strip

When a rule won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's own sentence at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused: ":

> Refused: track 3 is locked, so the gap on it cannot be closed

The strip shows up to three lines. Rest the pointer on it to read the whole sentence.

It stays until you click it or the project changes, which means an edit, an undo or redo, or going into or out of a nest. Moving the playhead or changing the selection doesn't clear it, so you can look around while you work out what to do.

The sentence is exact rather than friendly. It can name clips and tracks by Frame Job's own numbers, which aren't their positions on the timeline, and give lengths in the timeline's smallest units rather than in seconds.

Each feature's page lists what can stop it, and [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/) gathers them in one place.

A typed Start, Length or end value on an action shows the strip too. Dragging an action's band never does. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

## A drop that springs back

A clip dropped where the rules refuse animates back to where it was, and nothing changes. While you drag, positions that would be refused are skipped and the clip waits at the last allowed one. Only the drop counts. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).

## A beep with no message

An edit that would change nothing beeps but shows no message, because no rule was broken. A slip already at the end of the footage does this, and so does pasting a look the clips already have.

## An error alert

Now and then Frame Job can't use a request at all, such as a value outside its allowed range. It shows an error alert naming the offending value. You'll rarely meet one, because the inspector's number fields already [hold what you type to their range](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#type-a-value).

## With an agent

An agent gets the same answers as words. A refused edit fails with the rule's sentence, and an edit that changes nothing fails saying so. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

## Related

- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)
- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)

---
title: AI features and your own keys
description: Which features need nothing, which use an on-device model, which need your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, and what ever leaves your Mac.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Most of Frame Job needs no key and no network. The few features that send your words or audio to a cloud model run on your own API keys, so you decide what's used and you pay the provider directly.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where={['Settings ▸ Assistant', 'Settings ▸ Transcription']}
  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers']}
  needs="Your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, only for the features that send to them."
/>

## Your own keys

There's no Frame Job account and no relay in between. There are two keys in all, and each provider bills your account directly.

| Key | Turns on | Saved in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | The Assistant | [Settings ▸ Assistant](/assistant/set-up/) |
| AssemblyAI | Cloud captions and Remove Filler Words | [Settings ▸ Transcription](/captions/assemblyai-key/) |

Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each Assistant turn and each month costs. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). The provider's bill is the real figure.

With no key set, Settings says "No API key is set." in its ordinary muted colour. That's a state, not an error.

## What needs what

Anything that sends your words or audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.

| What it takes | Features |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing | Editing, colour, graphics, recording and export |
| An on-device model, with no key and no upload | **Generate Captions** with **On this Mac**, Remove Silences' voice analysis, Enhance Voice and Voice Isolation, Split at Shot Changes, Remove Background, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and Switch by Speaker |
| Your AssemblyAI key | The **AssemblyAI** engine of **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** with its **Transcribe** buttons |
| Your Anthropic key | The Assistant |

Filler removal works only through AssemblyAI. There's no on-device version.

Without your Anthropic key, **View ▸ Assistant** still opens the tab, which says how to add the key.

Work you've already paid for keeps working with no key:

- **Generate** isn't greyed when every file is already transcribed.
- **Remove Filler Words…** stays on while a file it would work on has a current transcript made with filler words.

An on-device language that isn't installed yet shows a **Download** row in the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet.

## Greyed commands

A command that needs a key you haven't set is greyed rather than hidden, and it says which key and where to set it.

A greyed menu item's title gains the key's name, as in **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. Rest the pointer on a greyed command or button and it reads:

> No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.

For the Assistant it's the same sentence with Anthropic and Assistant. The Assistant tab itself reads "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." with an **Open Settings…** button.

An agent's tool stops with the same sentence, at the point it would send. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what still works without a key.

## Saving a key takes effect at once

Saving or removing a key updates open sheets and menu items straight away. An open Generate Captions sheet turns **Generate** back on with the sheet still up, and there's nothing to reopen or relaunch.

## What stays on this Mac

Editing, analysis, on-device transcription, recording and export all stay on this Mac. Only these reach the network, and each is something you start or can see:

| Goes to | What | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AssemblyAI | The audio of the files being transcribed | When you press **Generate** or **Transcribe** with that engine. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/). |
| Anthropic | Your Assistant messages, the project's details and the frames it renders | While you use the Assistant. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/). |
| GitHub | A request for LiteLLM's published price table, with no key and no project data | At most once a day, from the Assistant's helper |
| GitHub | A check of the update feed | In the [downloaded copy](/getting-started/updates/) only |
| Apple | A request for an on-device speech model, through macOS | When you ask for one |

Frame Job has no analytics or telemetry code.

## Related

- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)

---
title: Updates
description: Check for a newer Frame Job, choose whether it checks by itself, and see which copies update themselves.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The copy of Frame Job you download keeps itself up to date. It tells you when a new version is ready and installs it only when you say so.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…"
  needs="The copy downloaded from the project's GitHub Releases page."
/>

## Which copy updates itself

The copy you download from the project's GitHub Releases page updates itself, with [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org). A copy built from source has no updater: it has no menu item and it never checks.

An update is always the whole app. Release notes are on the release's page on GitHub.

## Check for updates

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…**, directly under **About Frame Job**. It has no shortcut.

If a newer Frame Job has been published, a window shows its version and a link to its release page. Choose **Install Update** to replace the app and relaunch it. If there's nothing newer, it says you're up to date.

The item is greyed while a check is already running.

## Automatic checks

The second time you open Frame Job, it asks whether to check for updates automatically. If you agree, it checks about once a day while it's open and tells you when an update is ready. It never installs one without asking.

Frame Job [remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/) your answer and when it last checked.

## Turn automatic checks off

There's no Settings control for this. With Frame Job closed, run this in Terminal:

```sh
defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool NO
```

**Check for Updates…** still works afterwards.

## Signed updates

Every update is signed, and Frame Job refuses one whose signature doesn't match the key built into the app. Only a release published from the project itself can be installed.

## Good to know

No agent tool checks for updates or installs them.

## Related

- [Requirements and install](/getting-started/requirements-and-install/)
- [What stays on this Mac](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/#what-stays-on-this-mac)
- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)

13:/// a state in the muted colour, not an error. There is no Verify and no
model, and two settings for long conversations. The assistant itself is
described in [Assistant](assistant.md).

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or Return. | None |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | — |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Disabled when no key is stored. | — |
| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the assistant uses. Saved when you press Return or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000. | On, 300,000 |
| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn (never tool search results). | Off |
